newsitem.title: ANGOLA: U.N. announces start of withdrawal from Angola.
newsitem.headline: U.N. announces start of withdrawal from Angola.

text.p: The United Nations said on Thursday it would begin the wind-down of its 6,500-man peacekeeping operation in Angola next month.

"We will begin downsizing the peacekeeping operation from the end of December with the withdrawal of four companies of soldiers because some of the tasks have been completed," U.N. director for African peacekeeping operations, Hedi Annabi, told Reuters.
The withdrawal was expected to be completed by February 1997, Annabi said, as the international community could no longer afford to support the slow-moving peace process at $1 million a day.
"We will begin withdrawing the elements that are no longer needed here in Angola such as support teams including bridge- building companies and some infantry battalions," he added.
The U.N force has been overseeing the implementation of the Lusaka peace protocol signed two years ago.

On Thursday, a joint peace commission comprising the two Angolan factions plus observer states and the U.N. declared it was satisfied the government and the former rebel force UNITA had substantially complied with military tasks in the pact to end their two decades of civil war.
Annabi attended Thursday's sitting of the commission to review a timetable of military obligations set out by the U.N. Security Council for completion at midnight on Wednesday.

The U.N. Special Envoy to Angola, Alioune Blondin Beye, told a news conference: "The delegation unanimously concluded with great satisfaction that tasks set out by the Security Council have been completed...some 100 percent, others 80 percent, and others 75 percent."
From now on the commission would dedicate its time to implementing a political timetable which foresees a unity government, Beye said.
